title: What Is Tamper-Evident Audit Trail? Definition & Examples
snippet: A tamper-evident audit trail captures who invoked an AI agent, which tool it called, what policy decision was made, and when it happened, and is designed for forensic reconstruction, compliance review, and incident response. A tamper-evident audit trail is a record sequence engineered so that post-event changes, deletions, or gaps are detectable, preserving evidentiary value for AI agent actions, policy decisions, and tool invocations.

title: draft-sharif-agent-audit-trail-00 - Agent Audit Trail: A Standard Logging Format for Autonomous AI Systems
snippet: Records are linked via tamper-evident hash chaining using SHA-256 per RFC 8785, with optional ECDSA signatures for non-repudiation. The Agent Audit Trail (AAT) defines a JSON-based logging format with tamper-evident chaining, a defined action taxonomy, and explicit fields for agent identity, action classification, outcome tracking, and trust level reporting.

snippet: Blockchain technology is a distributed ledger system that creates an immutable record of transactions across a network of computers. Each transaction, or block, is cryptographically linked to the previous one, forming an immutable chain.

title: NIST Special Publication (SP) 800-92, Guide to Computer Security Log Management
snippet: At minimum each event should capture timestamp, event, status, and/or error codes, service/command/application name, user or system account associated with an event, and device used (such as source and destination IPs, terminal session ID, or web browser). title: Tamper-Evident Audit Trails for AI Agents: What SIEM Integration Actually Requires
snippet: The Agent Audit Trail format addresses requirements from the EU AI Act (Regulation 2024/1689), which mandates automatic recording of events for high-risk AI systems, and maps to SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria, ISO/IEC 42001, and PCI DSS v4.0.1 logging requirements.
